mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the signal, or 20-day forward returns in tightening periods are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% within a month indicates a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as consumer spending and business investment decline.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the signal, or 60-day forward returns in downturns are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP growth by more than 1% over two quarters signals a weakening demand environment, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings expectations are revised downwards.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 50% of periods with declining GDP, or 60-day forward returns in periods of GDP decline are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production by more than 2% within a month signals a strengthening supply side, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as increased production capacity supports economic growth.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the signal, or 20-day forward returns in periods of industrial production growth are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate falls below 4% and nonfarm payrolls increase by more than 200,000 in a month, it signals a tight labor market and strong economic growth, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as consumer confidence and spending increase.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4% and PAYEMS increases > 200k in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 50% of triggered instances despite the signal, or 5-day forward returns in periods of tight labor markets are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in housing starts by more than 10% within a month signals a strong demand for housing, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as increased construction activity boosts economic growth.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 50% of triggered instances despite the signal, or 20-day forward returns in periods of increased housing starts are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate is below 1% and the consumer price index increases by more than 0.5% in a month, it signals an inflationary environment with accommodative monetary policy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as investors seek higher returns in equities.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 1% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 50% of triggered instances despite the signal, or 60-day forward returns in inflationary periods with low rates are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption expenditures by more than 1% over two months signals a strengthening demand environment, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending boosts corporate earnings.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 50% of periods with increasing personal consumption, or 20-day forward returns in periods of consumption growth are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).
